headline: South Gippsland has had 14 earthquakes this month. A typical month there has none.
dek: The rest of Australia looks like a normal week. This page is not a warning.

cards.label: Gippsland, this month
cards.takeaway: A typical month here has none.

cards.label: Australia, this week
cards.takeaway: A usual week in and around Australia has about 11.

cards.label: Largest recent quake
cards.takeaway: 8 km NW of Leongatha, VIC. 3 October 2026, 3:01 am Melbourne time. About 21,700 people reported feeling it

cards.label: Heat near towns
cards.takeaway: 1,831 satellite detections were near towns over the last three days. These can be fires, or something else that is hot.

years.title: Gippsland's earthquakes stand out against 20 years
years.note: Each bar is a year of earthquakes of magnitude 2 or more near Leongatha. 17 have been recorded in 2026, and the year is not finished. 2009 and 2012 were busier still.

states.title: On land, most of the heat is in the north
states.note: Satellite detections over the last three days. Another 64,358 were offshore or not tied to a state. A detection is heat, not a confirmed bushfire.

sequence.title: The shaking near Leongatha has come in bursts
sequence.note: Each dot is one earthquake since 26 September. Higher means a larger quake.

meaning: If you are in South Gippsland, more small earthquakes may be felt for a while. If the ground shakes, drop, cover, and hold on.
A magnitude 4.9 quake near Leongatha on 3 October was widely felt. Feeling one earthquake does not mean a larger one is on the way.
Orange areas are satellite heat. They can be a bushfire or a false alarm. For what to do, use the official sources below. This page is not a warning service.
